summary:
THE MODEL, OPERATIONALLY. The thesis formalises a POD model M = <S, S0, SG, A, f, O> (methods.tex:91-103). States are base facts plus Know-If fluents over a finite Boxel partition; S0 holds one candidate state per Boxel the hidden target could occupy; the goal counts as reached only when the whole belief lies in SG; f is deterministic add/delete; O (the sensor model) is NOT inside the planner: it is a Python callable that reports found / not found at execution time and feeds the belief (methods.tex:102, 106). The single sense action (methods.tex:141-155) takes (?o ?region), requires view_clear(?region) and not-yet-known, and OPTIMISTICALLY asserts obj_at_boxel(?o,?region) plus the Know-If fluent; the live domain adds (handempty) and the hideability gate (boxel_fits ?o ?region) (domain_pddlstream.pddl:169-191). view_clear is a derived predicate: blocks_view_at(obj, boxel, region) are static geometric facts, blocks_view is derived from the object's current boxel, view_blocked = some blocker, view_clear = is_shadow and not view_blocked (domain_pddlstream.pddl:95-113). Sense calls no streams because the camera is fixed (methods.tex:170); the planner's only decisions about WHAT/WHERE/ORDER come from this search over region literals. Planning = one optimistic determinisation solved by PDDLStream + Fast Downward; execution runs the plan until a sense observation (ray-cast from the fixed camera) contradicts the assumption, then the belief is updated (found / known-empty / new occluder appended with its own shadow and the workspace re-boxelized) and the loop replans (methods.tex:157, 196-221). Termination is time-bounded: goal, no plan, every reachable region searched, or wall-clock budget (methods.tex:188; test_full_pipeline.py:1032-1037). Known unsoundnesses the thesis discloses: a relocated object casts no new shadow (methods.tex:26, 157; results.tex:439-444), and the 3-strike give-up: after three still-blocked senses the thesis says the shadow is marked as not containing the target, which violates belief-reflects-observation and is counted as a failure (methods.tex:168; results.tex:463-472). The live code has since changed that: the fragment is parked 'unresolved' and never asserted empty (execution.py:3061-3079; belief.py:22-33, 82-98), so the paper must describe the parked form, not the thesis wording. The thesis places the whole layer as a deliberately simplified POD planner (no contingent branching, no deductive axioms, unlike LW1) (results.tex:487-501).

THE TAMPURA CLAIMS. Every quantitative TAMPURA statement is INDIRECT: abstract.tex:18, results.tex:295/300/307-312/354, conclusion.tex:10 all state rough parity (144.4 s vs 166 s per episode; 65.6 % vs 55 % local or >= 63 % published-implied) while explicitly saying the two systems ran on different environments and the comparison 'benchmarks neither system'; results.tex:389-404 names the fix: 'Re-running both systems on a shared scene file would strengthen the comparison.' The architectural statements (results.tex:315-352; related-work.tex:14, 21, 22, 45, 47) are source-verified and stay true regardless of the bridge: TAMPURA learns a probabilistic sparse MDP online per step and solves it with LAO*; its Find Die keeps occlusion sub-symbolic (15 mm visibility voxels weight look success; placement is view-blind). One wording caveat carries over: released TAMPURA uses SymK (an FD top-k fork), so 'the same Fast Downward-based planner' means FD lineage, not the same search (THESIS_NOTES_HEAD.md:727-736). The bridge must deliver, seed for seed on TAMPURA's 20 seeds and their reward (holding(is-target) AND at-home, env.py:1004; rewards[-1]==1.0, sweep json metric_notes), per-episode end-to-end wall-clock for both systems on the same machine, planning-only time where separable, and honest failure counts, so that the parity sentences become measured rather than inferred.

WHAT STAYS THE THESIS'S METHOD. find_dice hides the die by CO-LOCATION under an upside-down cup; our lateral shadows never contain it (PAPER_AUDIT.txt:3184-3186). The honest extension is a REPRESENTATION one: a new region type (an enclosed/under-footprint volume hidden because an object of a known hollow class encloses it), entering the planner exactly like a shadow (a hidden region plus a blocks_view_at(cup, cup_boxel, region) fact, cleared by relocating the cup, sensed by the unchanged sense action). The thesis already names container interiors as a hidden region to be partitioned (conclusion.tex:35-45), so this is a disclosed direction, not a new method. If the fixed-camera model must be realised in their eye-in-hand world, a single fixed sensing configuration as a sense precondition is the degenerate form of the sensing-configuration extension the thesis also names (conclusion.tex:27-33) and must be reported as such. Adding at_home and a go_home action matches their goal and is a small domain extension. A scripted controller, a relaxed pick that bypasses streams (archived domain_find_dice.pddl:5-14), a bridge-internal arm-park that is not a planned action (#P4 (g)), welds/teleports (archive execution_bridge.py:27-35), belief writes that assert holding without a real grasp, or success scoring that ignores execution status (CB#123, archive boxel_policy.py:372-381) are NOT the method and were the failure that got the first bridge discarded.

LW1 / 3D WUMPUS DOOR. LW1 needs deterministic actions and sensing, observable variables with a precondition Pre(Y) and mutually exclusive state formulas W(Y=y), K-literal belief closed under axioms D', and optimistic assumption actions for selection (tools/lw1_text.txt:12-72). Our sense already has that shape (Y = 'target in region R', Pre = view_clear(R)). The bridge keeps the door open only if the belief stays literal-valued over named regions, observations stay deterministic functions of the world, no probability weights or planner-external choosers appear, and no region is ever asserted empty without an observation.

FROM THE PRIOR PLANS. Carry over: the occlusion caveat (containment vs lateral shadow; reveal structure identical: relocate -> sense -> pick -> home; their look is probabilistic in moved(occluder), ours is a hard precondition; TAMPURA_PLAN_HEAD.md:755-789), the unit corrections (57 s is per-step including sim execution, not per-episode; SymK; single-process; online learning), the seed-for-seed and never-edit-their-env rules, the scene facts (3 released layouts chosen by seed, cups first and die last in the JSON, die hidden relative to THEIR movable camera so fixed-camera validity must be re-checked), and the hideability-gate grounding risk found in the 2026-05-24 smoke test. Reject: the preset-in-our-framework route, the relaxed pick, the simplified weld pick, forced-success scoring, and any 'faithful' naming.

facts.claim: The formal POD model is M = <S, S0, SG, A, f, O>; S0 contains one candidate state per Boxel the hidden target could occupy; the task is solved only when the belief is contained in SG; O is realised as a Python callable outside the planner, which plans optimistically.
The thesis sense action has parameters (?o ?region), preconditions Obj, Boxel, view_clear, not obj_at_boxel_KIF, and effects obj_at_boxel_KIF, obj_at_boxel (optimistic found), obj_pose_known, cost 1.

The live domain's sense additionally requires (handempty) and (boxel_fits ?o ?region) (the hideability gate, --sense-gate off/strict via streams.test_target_can_hide_in_shadow); a cost-3 sense_partial variant was tried and withdrawn (F12).
view_clear is derived via stratified negation from static blocks_view_at facts and the object's current obj_at_boxel: blocks_view -> view_blocked -> view_clear = is_shadow and not view_blocked.
Sense calls no streams: the fixed camera means no sensing configuration is sampled; streams (sample-grasp, compute-kin, compute-stack-kin, plan-motion) serve manipulation only.

A target counts as hidden only when the camera's line of sight to every corner of its bounding box is blocked; visibility is any unobstructed corner ray; the oracle returns ground-truth identities and poses.

On a sense, the executor ray-casts from the fixed camera, updates the belief (target found, region known-empty, or a new occluder revealed and re-boxelized), and breaks to replan when the observation contradicts the optimistic assumption.
A relocated object is deliberately given no new shadow at its destination (termination concern); the shadow-blocker map is not recomputed at the new pose.
The loop is time-bounded, not replan-bounded: it ends on goal, planner no-plan, all reachable regions searched, or the per-cell wall-clock budget (1800 s in the thesis sweep).

Thesis wording of the 3-strike give-up: after three consecutive still-blocked senses the shadow is marked as not containing the target; this is stated as unsound (belief no longer reflects observation), accepted to bound the loop, distinguished in the run report, counted as a failure; the remedy (re-ground view-blocking atoms) is future work.

The live code no longer marks the shadow empty: after 3 strikes it calls belief.mark_unresolved, which parks the fragment ('unresolved', withheld from the planner) without asserting absence; the belief lifecycle is unknown -> not_here | found | unresolved.
Further 3-strike bounds exist in the live loop: pick_giveup (with up to 2 paroles after 4 replans), transit_loss, nontarget rediscovery (F9), physical stack failures (F28), drop_failed.

The thesis frames the planning layer as a deliberately simplified POD planner: PDDLStream and Fast Downward support neither contingent branching nor deductive axioms, so sense is optimistic with reactive replanning; LW1 would produce branching contingent plans with deductive axioms; the unsound give-up is 'one symptom'.

Belief is carried as a single Know-If fluent (obj_at_boxel_KIF) plus the value fluent obj_at_boxel, the PKS know-whether construct, logically equivalent to the K(p)/K(not p) pair for the boolean case.

Claim (indirect): the abstract states comparable end-to-end cost (about 144 s vs 166 s per episode) and comparable reliability (65.6 % vs >= 63 % implied by reported returns) against TAMPURA 'on the closest analogous hidden-object task', 'without learning a probabilistic policy'.

Claim (indirect): results.tex reports TAMPURA's published 57 +/- 38 s as per-step including sim execution; the local 20-seed Find Die re-run gives 166 +/- 85 s per successful episode vs our holding-semantic 144.4 s (median 21.6 s); per step about 11 s vs 57 s; reliability 65.6 % vs 55 % local / >= 63 % published-implied; 'on a marginally easier goal (Find Die also requires returning home)'; 'the two run on different environments, so it benchmarks neither system'.

Claim (explicit gap): 'we did not run TAMPURA on our own tabletop scenes: Find Die is the closest analogue, not the same problem'; Find Die ships three fixed scene layouts drawn at random per episode; both planners single-threaded; 'Re-running both systems on a shared scene file would strengthen the comparison.'

Claim (architectural): both systems sample geometry online and 'rely on the same determinised, Fast Downward-based classical planner'; TAMPURA's model-learning runs every control step and builds a probabilistic sparse MDP solved for a policy; the salient difference is that probabilistic layer.

Nuance for the paper: released TAMPURA uses SymK, a Fast Downward-derived top-k planner, so the shared element is the FD lineage / SAS+ translator, not the search strategy; 'do not claim an identical search engine'.

Claim (architectural): 'not a semantic-Boxels-beats-TAMPURA claim'; the comparison shows a deterministic replanning planner reaches the goal on the closest analogous task without estimating a learned sparse-MDP abstraction; both represent belief with symbolic atoms; the contrast is how knowledge is used.

Claim (architectural, source-backed): Find Die keeps occlusion sub-symbolic: a visibility voxel grid only weights the look action's success probability, and placement is sampled with no visibility check (view-blind); our planner flags view-blocking placements.
facts.evidence: thesis/chapters/results.tex:352; find_dice/env.py:36 (GRID_RESOLUTION=0.015), :966 (look depends=moved(?o2)), :307-321 (abstract emits known-pose/holding/at-home only); THESIS_NOTES_HEAD.md:740-747

facts.claim: Claim (indirect): 'a deterministic knowledge-literal planner with replanning is sufficient to reach the goal on this class of partially observable tabletop tasks (at comparable end-to-end cost and reliability, and simpler to model than TAMPURA's learned probabilistic policy)'.

Claims (architectural) in related work: TAMPURA's visibility grid weights look success (:14); learns a coarse abstract model, builds a non-deterministic MDP, solves with LAO* (:21); samples continuous placements and uses Bayes3D on the real robot (:22); keeps the spatial belief sub-symbolic so occluded regions are never named inspectable state (:45); three advantages with limitations, including 'optimistic determinise-and-replan is sound only while belief reflects observation' (:47).

Claim (indirect): the conclusion restates that the architectural comparison 'indicates that deterministic knowledge-literal planning with replanning reaches the goal at comparable end-to-end cost and reliability, without learning a probabilistic policy'.

The thesis names two extension hooks as future work: a sensing-configuration stream as an additional sense precondition (robot-mounted camera), and recursive partitioning of concave geometry whose interior 'is itself a hidden region' (container, cupboard).
Planning time (sum of PDDLStream call time) differs from the end-to-end per-episode wall-clock used in the TAMPURA comparison (134.30 s vs 144.4 s on holding-semantic).

TAMPURA find_dice operators: pick requires not moved(?o), not holding, known-pose(?o), object-grasp; place sets moved(?o) and known-pose; look(?o1,?o2,?q) depends on moved(?o2), requires looking-conf(?o2,?q), not known-pose(?o1), known-pose(?o2), not holding, verify_effects known-pose(?o1); go-home requires holding and not at-home; reward = Exists(is-target and holding) AND at-home.

Local TAMPURA run success criterion: rewards[-1] == 1.0 (die grasped AND at-home on the terminal belief); episodes run to max_steps=20 with no-ops; loop_s = time_deltas[-1] (planning + pybullet execution), wall_s includes process startup; config: bayes_optimistic, num_samples 200, num_skeletons 10, from_scratch true, gamma 0.98; aggregate 11/20 success, loop_s success 166.05 +/- 84.65 s.

#P4 record: the first bridge was discarded 2026-08-20 ('that work was trash. we should start over'), moved to archive/tampura_bridge_v1/; the restart must build on the post-#P1 weld-free pipeline; CB#120 state: (a) real streams, (b) RRT motion planning, (c) collision checking, (e) render+segmentation visibility were fixed; (d) hold still a JOINT_FIXED weld; (f) containment regions OPEN ('our lateral shadows never contain it... model cup-footprint containment regions'); (g) arm-park before sense is bridge-internal, not planned; (h) overlay perf.
CB#123 must-fix: the archived boxel_policy discarded execute_go_home's status and unconditionally marked at_home + success (no_path still scored reward 1.0); execute_pick ignored the lift status.

#P4 records PHASE 4 (gated >= 20-seed seed-for-seed eval on their exact seeds, honest failures included) as the replacement for the thesis's indirect comparison, and records the no-op-policy harness (drives their env, belief and reward untouched) as acceptable, with native action-schema execution via their effects_fn/execute_fn optional.

Archived bridge shortcuts (the failure to never repeat): execute_simplified_pick teleports the object into the gripper and welds it (resetBasePositionAndOrientation + createConstraint); _weld createConstraint in execution_boxel; belief_bridge writes current_conf = DEFAULT_ARM_POS into their SceneBelief; the archived domain variant RELAXED pick to ground without IK/grasp streams and added an at_sense_config precondition; SENSE_ARM_CONF hardcoded to DEFAULT_ARM_POS.

Occlusion caveat (prior plan): find_dice occludes by CONTAINMENT (die at the cup's pose under an upside-down cup, revealed by moving the cup; look success depends on moved(occluder)); ours by LATERAL shadow; the reveal structure is parallel (clear occluder -> sense -> pick -> home); residual differences to state: mode, probabilistic look vs hard view_clear precondition, give-up rule; 'the defensible comparison is on the TASK... realised in each system's native occlusion model'.

Prior corrections now binding: SymK is an FD top-k fork (not 'SymK vs FD'); TAMPURA is single-process (core-count framing overstated); 57 +/- 38 s is PER-STEP incl. sim controller execution (not per-episode, not planning-only); holding is not find_dice (at-home missing); model learning is ONLINE per step (no offline framing); 'TAMPURA trades success for speed' was unverified.

Smoke findings on our own env (2026-05-24): the planner deliberately relocates an occluder, senses, and picks in one plan with no give-up (default scene seed 0); a lone small occluder fails to ground because test_target_can_hide_in_shadow over-covers the occlusion cone (no fully occluded candidate -> boxel_fits absent -> 0 skeletons); a 2-occluder decoy scene grounds but collides during relocation and stalls in slow replanning.

PHASE 3B risks recorded: released scenes were hidden relative to THEIR movable wrist camera, so under a fixed camera some may be trivial or unsolvable (re-validate and record); our oracle assumed the default pybullet client; the scene JSON lists cups first and 'dice' last, index-aligned with poses; seed 0 selects a 1-cup scene; the global seed picks one of 3 problem JSONs by random.choice.

#P9: full POD planning (compile PDDLStream groundings into LW1, gaining contingent plans and deductive axioms) then a 3D Wumpus-style domain; justified by TH#238/239/248/307/328; 'the unsound 3-strike bounded give-up is the visible symptom'; CB#105 Wumpus baseline is the first rung; post-deadline unless #P1-#P4 finish early.

LW1 model requirements: P = <V, I, G, A, W>; W has observable variables Y with Pre(Y) and mutually exclusive state formulas W(Y=y) in positive DNF; completeness holds for width-1 problems with deterministic actions and sensing; belief tracking uses K-literals closed under axioms D' (Kx => OR of K-not-x' etc.) with unit resolution on observations; action selection H(P) adds assumption actions (optimism) and deduction actions.

THESIS_NOTES speed caveats: both single-threaded; per-thread hardware favours the host; TAMPURA is anytime; neither system caches across episodes; a TAMPURA 'step' re-solves per control action whereas our plan solves once for many actions (per-step axis is softer); the notes' 13.7 s / 42 % figures are pre-CB#107 and superseded by the thesis's 144.4 s / 65.6 %.

#P1 permits exactly one hardcoded motion: the lift after a pick or place (collision-avoidance aid); welds, release teleports, oracle pose reads, id-matched ray classification, and planning-time ground-truth AABB reads are all listed to go.
The current Boxel type system has exactly OBJECT, SHADOW and FREE_SPACE.

The thesis's observation model is gated on line of sight ('the percept rides on the action that establishes its precondition', Wumpus analogy): a shadow whose view stays blocked yields no observation and cannot become known-empty by repetition.

The thesis says PDDLStream/FD support no 'deductive axioms', yet the domain uses PDDL :derived predicates for view_clear; the intended meaning is LW1-style knowledge axioms (D'), so paper wording should say 'knowledge/deductive axioms over K-literals' to avoid a reviewer catching the derived predicates.

design_relevant_details: Sense action signature (thesis and live domain): (:action sense :parameters (?o ?region) :precondition (and (Obj ?o) (Boxel ?region) (handempty) (view_clear ?region) (not (obj_at_boxel_KIF ?o ?region)) (boxel_fits ?o ?region)) :effect (and (obj_at_boxel_KIF ?o ?region) (obj_at_boxel ?o ?region) (obj_pose_known ?o) (increase (total-cost) 1))); the bridge domain must keep this action unchanged (domain_pddlstream.pddl:169-191).

Visibility derivation chain to reuse for any new region type: static (blocks_view_at ?obj ?b ?region) in init; (:derived (blocks_view ?obj ?region) ...) from (obj_at_boxel ?obj ?b); (:derived (view_blocked ?region) (exists blocker)); (:derived (view_clear ?region) (and (is_shadow ?region) (not (view_blocked ?region)))) (domain_pddlstream.pddl:95-113). A containment region = a region with is_shadow-equivalent status plus blocks_view_at(cup, cup_boxel, region).

Belief API (belief.py): BeliefState(shadows, target); shadow_status in {'unknown','not_here','found','unresolved'}; mark_sensed(shadow_id, found); mark_unresolved(shadow_id); get_parked_shadows(); add_shadow/remove_shadow; mark_occluder_moved(occluder_id, destination). Any containment region must be registered here so all-searched exits stay honest (belief.py:40-98).

BoxelType enum: OBJECT, SHADOW, FREE_SPACE (boxel_data.py:18-22). A containment/enclosed region needs either a new enum member or a SHADOW subtype flag; planner init emits is_shadow for sensing regions (pddlstream_planner.py ~718-742 emits marginally_blocked and derived-predicate facts).

Hideability gate: streams.test_target_can_hide_in_shadow (3x3 grid, 8 AABB corners, fully occluded, table-resting) controls whether (boxel_fits ?o ?region) is emitted for a sense region; --sense-gate off emits for every pair, strict only where the target class fits fully occluded (domain_pddlstream.pddl:177-183; TAMPURA_PLAN_HEAD.md:647-658). For a cup-interior region the fit test must be geometric (die fits under the cup footprint), not a camera ray test.

Give-up constants: blocked_counts threshold 3 (execution.py:3061); pick strikes 3 with parole after 4 replans and at most 2 paroles (test_full_pipeline.py:1057-1078); transit_loss 3; nontarget rediscovery 3; stack failures 3 (test_full_pipeline.py:1079-1104). All are executor-side bounds, not planner logic; the bridge must keep them disclosed per episode.

TAMPURA success criterion to adopt verbatim: reward = And([Exists(is-target(?o) and holding(?o)), at-home]) evaluated on their belief (env.py:993-1004); at-home == np.allclose(current_conf, DEFAULT_ARM_POS) (PHASE3B:53); success iff rewards[-1] == 1.0 (sweep json metric_notes).

TAMPURA timing fields to compare like-for-like: loop_s = RolloutHistory.time_deltas[-1] (planning + execution inside the policy loop), wall_s = full process; published 57 +/- 38 s is per-step incl. controller execution; local success-only loop_s 166.05 +/- 84.65 s (n=11), all 239.90 +/- 151.09 s (n=20) (sweep json:788-833).

TAMPURA scene schema: problems/*.json {categories: [... '*_cups_ud' ..., 'dice'], poses: [[xyz],[quat]] index-aligned}; cups first, 'dice' last; die XY == hiding cup XY; 1-5 cups, one hides the die; 3 released JSONs selected by random.choice under the global seed (PHASE3B:60-67, 158-162; TAMPURA_PLAN_HEAD.md:54-62).

TAMPURA camera is eye-in-hand (look_execute_fn env.py:523 plans arm motion to a look conf; look_sample_fn :584); our model needs ONE fixed viewpoint. Options the thesis can absorb: a fixed external camera observer added bridge-side (perception only, their dynamics untouched) or a single fixed sensing arm config as a sense precondition (the degenerate case of conclusion.tex:27-33's sensing-configuration extension); either must be reported as a model difference.

Our goal for the bridge must be (and (holding die) (at_home)) with a go_home action and at_home fluent added to the domain variant to match Find Die (TAMPURA_PLAN_HEAD.md:579-580, 704-705); the thesis's holding goal alone is 'marginally easier' (results.tex:295).

Only permitted hardcoded motion: the post-pick/post-place lift (PAPER_AUDIT.txt:132-133; results.tex:428-432). An arm-park before sense must be a planned move action or a domain precondition, never bridge-internal logic (#P4 (g)).

Thesis success accounting to preserve: a run is a success only if a physics check confirms the goal holds after settling; symbolic-only successes are 'false success' and count as failures (methods.tex:184; results.tex:96).

Planning-time metric (sum of PDDLStream call time, results.tex:93) and end-to-end per-episode wall-clock must both be logged for ours; for TAMPURA only loop_s/wall_s and SymK solve times are separable (sweep json metric_notes).

Prior P1 perception strategy: our perception reads THEIR live pybullet world via an adapter on the default client (client id 0 created first by env.initialize); a mirror world (P2) adds clients and breaks the default-client assumption (PHASE3B:303-318, 564-579).

Budget mismatch to decide: TAMPURA episodes end at max_steps=20 (no wall-clock cap); our cells use a 1800 s wall-clock budget (results.tex:85). The comparison must fix and report one budget rule per system.

LW1 shape to keep: observable variable Y_R = 'target in region R' with Pre(Y_R) = view_clear(R) and W(found) = obj_at_boxel(o,R); belief literals over a finite region set; deterministic observation function of the true world (ray-cast/render against actual geometry).
honesty_risks: Reading the die's true pose (their State world, problems/*.json poses, or their SceneBelief.object_poses) to decide which cup to move, where to sense, or whether the die is 'found': that is the oracle read H1 forbids. The containment region must be derived from the CUP's geometry and class, never from the die.

Hardcoding the search order or the target cup ('cup_0', 'the only cup', 'move cup then sense then pick'): with 1-cup scenes the plan is trivial, which tempts a scripted sequence; the planner must still emit relocate -> sense -> pick -> go_home from the belief (H2, H4).

A relaxed pick/place that grounds without the grasp/IK/motion streams (the archived domain_find_dice.pddl did this): it removes the planner's geometric reasoning and is the slide into 'main movement up to the planner, everything else scripted'.
Bridge-internal arm-park before each sense (#P4 (g)): an unplanned motion decision; make it a planned move or a sense precondition in the domain and report it.

Marking a cup-interior region empty without observing it (by rule, by strike count, or because 'the die must be under the other cup'): closes the LW1 door and repeats the F15 belief lie; only the parked 'unresolved' form is acceptable and must be disclosed.

Writing holding/at-home into their SceneBelief without a real grasp or without the arm actually at DEFAULT_ARM_POS, or ignoring execute_* statuses (CB#123): forced success. Success must come from their reward on a belief that reflects a physically verified grasp and pose.

Welds (createConstraint) or teleports (resetBasePositionAndOrientation) for the pick, hold, or release: the bridge must use the post-#P1 friction grasp and motor release; the archived execute_simplified_pick and _weld are the exact anti-patterns.

Adding a fixed external camera to their world and calling the environment 'untouched': it is a perception-side addition and a sensing-model difference from their eye-in-hand look; it must be an audit entry with before/after, not silent.

Comparing our planning-only time against their loop_s, or quoting their 57 s per-step against our per-episode: unit errors already made twice (TH#213). Report end-to-end per episode on the same machine as primary; per-step only with the step-definition caveat.
Treating 20 seeds as 20 scenes: their seed selects one of 3 released layouts; the paper must say so (results.tex:394-397) and the bridge must not special-case any layout.

Validating scenes under our fixed camera and silently dropping the ones where the die is visible or unreachable: every seed must be run and its outcome counted; scene-validity findings go in the record, not in a filter.

Probabilistic shortcuts (weighting cups by likelihood, learned priors, reading TAMPURA's belief probabilities) to pick a cup: departs from the literal POD belief and from the thesis's claim (ii) 'uncertainty is handled without probabilities'.
Post-processing the plan (reordering, inserting go_home, dropping actions) between solve() and the executor: forbidden by H2; fix plan quality in the domain or report the plan as is.
Describing the give-up in paper prose with the thesis wording ('marked empty') when the code parks it unresolved, or the reverse; and reusing 'faithful' in any new identifier or prose (H6).

Hideability/sense gates tuned to pass on cup geometry (e.g. loosening test_target_can_hide_in_shadow only for the bridge): a scene-specific gate change is seed/scene-specific code by another name; any gate change must apply to the main pipeline too and get its own audit entry.
open_questions: Fixed viewpoint in their eye-in-hand world: a bridge-side fixed external camera, or sensing only from one fixed arm configuration whose wrist camera is the viewpoint? Which does the user consider 'their env untouched', and how is it worded in the paper?

Containment region geometry: is the die's AABB inside the cup's OBJECT boxel (co-located), so the enclosed volume must be carved out of the cup boxel as its own region, and does the post-#P1 perception (render + segmentation) register the cup as a single body whose interior is unobserved?

Which cup class is 'a certain kind of object'? Category labels ('*_cups_ud') are available from the scene spec in both systems; is using the category label as an is_container predicate acceptable, or must hollowness be inferred from the mesh/AABB?

How does the hideability gate (test_target_can_hide_in_shadow) behave for a cup-footprint region that is enclosed rather than camera-shadowed, and does the sense gate need an 'enclosed' branch that applies to the main pipeline as well?

Does any released layout have more than one cup, so the planner's choice of which cup to relocate is non-trivial across the 20 seeds? If all three layouts have one cup, what can the comparison honestly claim about search?

Execution harness: the no-op policy writing into their SceneBelief (recorded as acceptable in #P4) vs native action-schema execution through their effects_fn/execute_fn; which does the user want given the discarded bridge's history?

Budget rule for the comparison: their max_steps=20 vs our 1800 s wall-clock; should ours also be capped by a step count, and how are TAMPURA failures (ran to max_steps) matched against our give-up exits?
